observations.skeptic_problem: None. The 'by construction' caveat is correct. In addition, seq order has 0/10012 inversions because seq is itself time-ordered, so the export's 'revision order failures = 0' check is tautological.
observations.skeptic_numbers: Ordering violations 0/14482 (req<=succ), 0/14482 (req<=write_date), 0/14482 (req<=archived), 0/14585 (succ<=archived), 0/14591 (write_date<=archived); Wilson upper bound 0.00027. time==write_date 14591/14591; time==request_time 14482/14482; time==success_time 12884/14585. success-request {0:12792, 1:1689, 2:1}. Deletes success-request {0:4746, 1:470}; clock_delta mismatches 0/5216. Revision seq order vs time: 0/10012 inversions, so seq is time-sorted by construction.
observations.statement: No physically required clock ordering is violated inside collusion-wiki. The 5 checked orderings are request<=success, request<=write_date, request<=archived_at, success<=archived_at and write_date<=archived_at. Much of this agreement is by construction: time, write_date and request_time are identical on every row, so they are one clock written three times.
observations.numbers: Violations 0/14482, 0/14482, 0/14482, 0/14585, 0/14591; Wilson upper bound 0.0003 each. time==write_date 14591/14591; time==request_time 14482/14482. success_time - request_time values {0: 12792, 1: 1689, 2: 1}, n=14482. Deletes: success - request {0: 4746, 1: 470}; clock_delta_seconds mismatches 0/5216.
observations.mechanical_explanation: The export joined request-log rows to saves by exact time equality and passed its own 'revision order failures = 0' check. Only success_time (0-2 s) and archived_at are independent of the save time.

observations.skeptic_problem: Minor overclaim. 'All on 4 heavily edited shared pages' is really 68/72 on one page (dse/WillkommenImWiki), plus 1-2 each on 3 other pages, one of which is a single-agent probe page. The race explanation is plausible but untested.
observations.skeptic_numbers: 72/10012 adjacent RCS-minor pairs with decreasing time; Wilson [0.0057, 0.0090]; page-clustered [0.0001, 0.0146], 1453 pages. Magnitudes {-1:13, -2:29, -3:28, -4:1, -5:1}. Label differs 70/72, ip16 differs 71/72. rcs minor != seq: 414 revisions on 5 pages. Per page: WillkommenImWiki 68, OAIResearchBridgeMay3X 2, AgentOurIvyProbe1781643368 1, StartSeite 1.
observations.statement: POST-HOC. RCS commit order (the 1.N storage sequence) disagrees with timestamp order on 72 adjacent pairs, all on 4 heavily edited shared pages. All inversions are 1-5 s, and nearly every inverted pair involves two different labels and ip16.
observations.numbers: 72/10012 = 0.0072, Wilson [0.0057, 0.0090]; page-clustered [0.000, 0.015], 1453 pages. 59 inversions exceed 1 s. Magnitudes {-1: 13, -2: 29, -3: 28, -4: 1, -5: 1}. Labels differ in 70/72 pairs, ip16 differs in 71/72. Separately, 414/14591 revisions on 5 pages have an RCS minor number different from seq.
observations.mechanical_explanation: Concurrent saves to the same page: the timestamp is taken before the commit lock, so commit order and timestamp order can swap by a few seconds. This is a race, not fabrication.

observations.skeptic_problem: OVERCLAIM and MISLABEL. (1) 'Far more common than at nearby shifted times' is false at the hour scale. The windows at +-2h and -4h score 0.47-0.54 against 0.566 observed. The 0.259 local-null excess comes mostly from the +-1d shifts, which are ~0 for single-day sources. The honest local excess is about 0.10 (+-2h/4h), or about 0.03 against the immediately preceding hours. (2) The per-source numbers in the statement (SEC 0.423, USAspending 0.369, MAX 0.393, Clark 0.675, IHME 0.595) are excess over the local null, not before-window rates. Placed next to 'Before-window at 1 h: 0.566', they read as rates; the true before rates are 0.994, 0.764, 0.833, 0.800 and 0.909. (3) The page-clustered CI understates uncertainty, because events on different pages share one campaign burst; the source-day-clustered CI is [0.094, 0.894]. The core claim reproduces: day/campaign-level co-activity that is source-specific (permutation excess about 0.33). It is not hour-level precedence.
observations.skeptic_numbers: My own patterns (raw substrings only, no URL-decoding) give 3044 new-mention events on 2063 pages; the lens has 3116 on 2223 because it also matches decoded proxy URLs. Before-window 1h: 0.555 [0.449, 0.671] page-clustered. Local null (+-2h/4h/1d) 0.305; excess 0.250 [0.204, 0.298]. Permutation null 0.224; excess 0.331. 24h excess over local null 0.146 [0.138, 0.153]. KEY CHECKS: (a) The lens's own per-shift rates are -2h 0.536, +2h 0.473, -4h 0.510, +4h 0.302, but +-1d 0.009/0.011. The local-null 'excess' is therefore driven by the +-1d shifts, which are near 0 by construction because SEC county's 455 reports all fall on 2026-06-18 (04:23-23:27Z). With a +-2h/4h-only null, my excess is 0.102 [0.087, 0.116] page-clustered and [0.042, 0.181] with 36 source-day clusters. With +-2h only it is 0.059; against the two preceding hours it is 0.030 [0.020, 0.044]. (b) My hourly profile, P(report in the 1h window ending at t+k h), for k = -3..3: 0.523, 0.526, 0.538, 0.555, 0.536, 0.466, 0.477. This is a broad multi-hour plateau with a peak of about 0.02 at the hour before the save. (c) Clustering by source-day (36 clusters) instead of page widens before-obs to 0.555 [0.094, 0.894]. (d) SEC county is 45% of events, 80% of before-window hits and 74% of the local-null excess. Its before rate is 0.996 and its after rate is 0.925 (lens). (e) Per source, the lens JSON shows these before/after rates: MAX 0.833/0.859, IHME 0.909/0.932, Clark 0.800/1.000. Only USAspending (0.764/0.558) leans 'before'. My per-source excess over the +-2h/4h null: SEC 0.123, USAspending 0.214, MAX 0.202, Clark 0.599, IHME 0.438.
observations.statement: When a wiki page first names a catalog data source, a urlquery report for that same source in the preceding hour is far more common than at nearby shifted times or with sources permuted. The two independent witnesses agree on which source was being worked when.
observations.numbers: Before-window at 1 h: 0.566 [0.481, 0.655], n=3116 events on 2223 pages (page-clustered). Nulls: +-7/14 d shift 0.000 [0.000, 0.001]; source permutation 0.233 [0.182, 0.291]; post-hoc local +-2h/4h/1d 0.307 [0.264, 0.352]. Excess over the local null 0.259 [0.217, 0.303]; over the permutation null 0.332 [0.298, 0.365]. Excess over the local null at 24 h: 0.147 [0.140, 0.153]. Per source at 1 h: SEC county 0.423 [0.396, 0.445] (n=1432); USAspending 0.369 (n=165); MAX 0.393 (n=78); Clark 0.675 (n=60); IHME 0.595 (n=44).
observations.mechanical_explanation: This is campaign-level co-activity, not a link from a specific claim to a specific fetch. SEC county data is 1432 of the 3116 events, and all 455 of its reports fall on one UTC day. 8 of the 52 catalog methods were chosen partly from wiki content (urlquery_methods_with_wiki_in_reason). That makes source selection wiki-informed, though the report times are a census of each query.

observations.skeptic_problem: None for the null conclusion: directionality is weak under both event definitions. The point estimate is sensitive to the event set (0.019 vs 0.042). The reverse-direction numbers were not checked.
observations.skeptic_numbers: Forward before-minus-after 1h: 0.019 [0.010, 0.027] (n=3044, 2063 pages; lens 0.042 on its 3116-event set). 24h: 0.161 [0.109, 0.215] (lens 0.159). I did not re-derive the reverse burst direction.
observations.statement: Directionality is weak. A source report is only slightly more likely before a wiki mention than after it, and a urlquery burst is only slightly more likely to be followed by a wiki mention than the local null predicts.
observations.numbers: Forward, before minus after: 0.042 [0.010, 0.078] at 1 h; 0.159 [0.115, 0.204] at 24 h (n=3116, 2223 pages). Reverse, burst followed by a wiki mention within 1 h: 0.085 [0.019, 0.159], local null 0.045, excess 0.040 [0.007, 0.079] (n=4935 bursts, 131 source-days). Reverse excess at 24 h: 0.031 [-0.015, 0.085].
observations.mechanical_explanation: Both witnesses record overlapping streams of activity on the same source (median lag back to the prior report 971 s, forward to the next report 491.5 s), so there is no clean fetch-then-write ordering.

observations.skeptic_problem: None material. CYBR is 5 vs 9 because of URL-decoding. 'A missing report is not evidence of fabrication' is a fair caution; the data cannot say the fetches were real.
observations.skeptic_numbers: DataUSA before 1h: 48/1259 = 0.038 [0.028, 0.049], 1203 pages. 91 DataUSA reports on 8 days; 14 mention days, 3 overlapping (500 mentions on overlap days). US Census API: 0/58 events (17 pages), 5 reports on 3 days (2026-05-12, 05-24, 06-03), 0 overlap days. Yahoo CYBR: 5 events with 0 catalog reports under my pattern (lens 9, with decoded matching).
observations.statement: urlquery coverage depends on the source. For DataUSA and the US Census API, wiki mentions are almost never preceded by a report, so a missing report is not evidence that a claimed fetch was fabricated.
observations.numbers: DataUSA before-window at 1 h: 0.038 [0.028, 0.049], n=1259 events on 1203 pages; 91 DataUSA reports in the catalog in total. US Census API: 0/58 at every window; 5 catalog reports, 0 days overlapping with wiki mentions. 9 mention events belong to a source with 0 catalog reports (Yahoo CYBR).
observations.mechanical_explanation: The agents had other fetch paths (direct requests, other proxies), and urlquery is one optional route.

observations.skeptic_problem: PARTIAL OVERCLAIM. Same-second co-occurrence is a real excess (9810 vs 3381-5346 under uniform-within-bin nulls). But 'almost all same-second groups contain a single source' is mostly compositional: shuffling sources within the same minute already gives 3899/4130 (94%) single-source, so the excess homogeneity is about 99 groups (2.4 percentage points). Single-source groups are dominated by UNCTAD (2389/3998). The batch-submission explanation is not distinguished from scanner-side queue batching.
observations.skeptic_numbers: Same-second histogram {1:28350, 2:3051, 3:744, 4:231, 5:73, 6:30, 7:1}; 9810/38160 reports in groups >=2; 4130 multi-report groups, 3998 single-source, 132 mixed. Zero gaps 5680/38159, median gap 10 s. 60s bursts 8078 (3828 singletons, max 1006); multi-report bursts 3410 single-source, 840 mixed. NULLS I added: the source-homogeneity count expected from local temporal composition (sources shuffled within bin) is 2651 (day), 3561 (hour), 3689 (10 min) and 3899 (minute), against 3998 observed. Same-second clustering itself exceeds a uniform-within-bin null: reports in groups 3381 (60 s bins) and 5346 (10 s bins), against 9810 observed.
observations.statement: urlquery timestamps cluster at the same second, and almost all same-second groups contain a single data source.
observations.numbers: Same-second group sizes {1: 28350, 2: 3051, 3: 744, 4: 231, 5: 73, 6: 30, 7: 1}; 9810/38160 reports sit in a group of 2 or more. 3998/4130 multi-report groups have one source; 132 mix sources. Zero gaps 5680/38159; median gap 10 s. 60 s bursts: 8078, of which 3828 are singletons; maximum size 1006. Multi-report bursts: 3410 single-source, 840 mixed.
observations.mechanical_explanation: Most likely batch submission by programs: one script submits many URLs for one source at once. That is consistent with the custom_program / indirection classes. The second-of-minute chi-square p=1.3e-4 is not interpretable because the reports are not independent.

observations.skeptic_problem: None for the asymmetry. It reproduces with a different keyword set and window. The class sizes differ from the lens (task 1835 vs 6105, unqualified 6911 vs 4238) because of keyword lists, and the conclusion is unchanged. Minor overclaim: a median of about -80 s mixes clock offset with compose/POST latency, so it does not by itself show the save clock is UTC 'to within about a minute'. O10's -1 s is the stronger cross-check.

New per-revision claims, folded to [-12h, 12h). Real: n=738, 242 pages, median -77 s [-98, -60]; [-1h,0) 544 vs (0,1h] 87. With seconds only: n=510, median -64 s [-105, -46], 376 vs 53. Task: n=1835, 109 vs 110. Unqualified: n=6911, 372 vs 351.
observations.statement: Narrated wall-clock times ('UTC', 'terminal', 'container') sit just before the save that carries them, whereas task-clock times are spread evenly around the save. This shows that the keyword classifier separates real clock readings from task-clock times.
observations.numbers: Real-clock time-of-day claims: n=854 new claims on 263 pages; median delta -84 s, page-clustered [-107.5, -64]. Counts in [-1h,0) vs (0,+1h]: 601 vs 95. observations.mechanical_explanation: None found. It also cross-validates that the wiki 'time' field is UTC to within about a minute.

observations.skeptic_problem: The headline rate reproduces approximately (0.188 vs 0.211). The tense-split null rests on a post-hoc keyword tagger, which I did not check.
observations.skeptic_numbers: Real-clock claims more than 1 s after the save: 139/738 = 0.188, Wilson [0.162, 0.218]. I did not reproduce the post-hoc tense split.
observations.statement: The test 'a claim about an event cannot postdate its own save' does not separate cleanly for time-of-day claims. Of the 21% of real-clock claims that postdate their save, most are projections. Among past- or present-tense claims, the near-future rate is no higher than the task-clock control or a uniform unrelated clock.
observations.numbers: 180/854 real-clock claims are more than 1 s after the save: 0.211 [0.178, 0.245]. POST-HOC by tense: forward-looking 70/164 after the save. Past or present tense, not approximate: near-future band (1 s, 1 h] 7/125 = 0.056 [0.017, 0.100] (82 pages); task-clock control 37/550 = 0.067 [0.042, 0.095]; uniform expectation 0.042.

observations.skeptic_problem: None. The prose n is lower (582 vs 747) because I excluded ms/us/ns forms and applied a range filter; the conclusion is identical. Selection caveat: epochs that get written into pages probably come from scripts that print time.time() and save right away.
observations.skeptic_numbers: Prose epochs (10-digit, within +-365 d of the save, outside an http/www URL): n=582, 285 pages, median -1 s [-1, -1]; 7/582 more than 1 s after the save (0.012 [0.006, 0.025]). With fraction: 0/459, Wilson upper bound 0.0083 (exact match to the lens). Without fraction: 7/123. Page-name epochs vs first save: n=385, 173 labels, median -2 s [-3, -2].
observations.statement: Epochs printed from a real clock never postdate the save that carries them. Agent sandbox clocks agree with the wiki server clock to about 1-2 s.
observations.numbers: Epochs in prose: n=747 on 297 pages, median delta -1 s [-1, -1]; 10/747 = 0.013 [0.005, 0.025] more than 1 s after the save. POST-HOC: with a fractional part (time.time() form) 0/459, Wilson upper bound 0.008, median -1 s; without a fraction 10/288. Epochs in page names (vs the first save): n=396, 183 labels, median -2 s [-3, -2].
observations.mechanical_explanation: None for the 0/459. NTP-synced sandboxes are expected.

observations.skeptic_problem: Counts reproduce, and the effect does not depend on the exact roundness rule. The interpretation 'agents wrote a guessed now without reading a clock' overclaims. Half the round after-save stamps are hours to weeks ahead, which fits hand-picked round identifiers (1782000000, 1783000000) better than guesses of now. Effective independence is low: 9 labels, 18/26 from a single anonymous label. It remains post-hoc, as the lens says.
observations.skeptic_numbers: Page-name epochs: round (mod100 in {0,1,99}) 26/54 more than 1 s after the first save, label-clustered 0.481 [0.152, 0.667], 33 labels. Non-round 5/331, 0.015 [0.000, 0.022]. Near-future (1 s, 1h]: round 13/54 = 0.241 [0.091, 0.333]; non-round 2/331. Prose round 6/27 vs non-round 1/555. The 26 round after-save cases are 26 distinct epochs from 9 labels, 18 of them from the anonymous probier label ''. Their deltas run from 15 s to 1,333,479 s: 13/26 are more than 1h ahead and 6/26 more than 1 day ahead (e.g. 1782000000, 1783000000). Robust to the roundness definition: mod10==0 18/71 vs 13/314; mod1000==0 11/17 vs 20/368. Round values are 54/385 = 14% of page-name epochs, against 3% expected for uniform last digits.
observations.statement: POST-HOC, definition chosen after seeing examples. Epoch-like stamps that postdate their own save are concentrated among round numbers (ending in 00, 01 or 99), which suggests agents wrote a guessed 'now' without reading a clock.
observations.numbers: Page names more than 1 s after the first save: round 26/55 = 0.473 (label-clustered [0.118, 0.660], 34 labels) vs non-round 5/341 = 0.015 ([0.000, 0.022], 153 labels). Near-future band (1 s, 1 h]: round 0.236 [0.088, 0.316] vs non-round 0.006 [0.000, 0.016]. Prose epochs: round 6/37 = 0.162 [0.049, 0.303] vs non-round 4/710 = 0.006 [0.000, 0.013].
observations.mechanical_explanation: Contaminated: the 20 inspected examples that suggested the roundness rule are inside the 26/55. Other possible causes: loop counters on a hand-picked base (e.g. ...000, ...001), or intended future markers. Needs a holdout.

observations.skeptic_problem: The direction reproduces (URL epochs postdate the save more often than prose), but my n differs (125 vs 370) and so does the >1 day count (3 vs 30). The lens includes 13/16/19-digit forms with no range filter, so its '30 more than a day ahead' depends on those forms. I did not verify the signed-URL expiry explanation.
observations.skeptic_numbers: 10-digit, +-365 d, http/www URL spans: URL epochs n=125 on 50 pages; 11/125 more than 1 s after the save (0.088, page-clustered [0.009, 0.198]); only 3 more than 1 day after. Round 2/15 vs non-round 9/110.
observations.statement: Epoch stamps inside URLs postdate the save far more often, and mostly by more than a day.
observations.numbers: 39/370 = 0.105 [0.021, 0.231] page-clustered (81 pages) more than 1 s after the save; 30 of them more than 1 day after. Round 3/38 vs non-round 36/332.
observations.mechanical_explanation: Server-generated expiry tokens in signed URLs, and agent-made incrementing 'uniq=' sequences on a far-future base. This is why URL epochs were pre-registered as a separate class.

observations.statement: POST-HOC exploratory. Narrated task-clock to UTC mappings are not self-consistent at the minute level within a label.
observations.numbers: 482 new mapping pairs on 162 pages. Labels with at least 2 distinct pairs: 84; median offset spread 6268 s. Spread <=60 s: 3/84 = 0.036 [0.012, 0.100]. Spread <=600 s: 18/84 = 0.214 [0.140, 0.314].
observations.mechanical_explanation: The task clock may not run at wall-clock rate, a label may span several cohorts or episodes, or the nearest-time pairing heuristic may mis-pair. Untested.

observations.statement: The one exact urlquery report cited in the wiki is consistent with physical order: the citing revision comes after the report. Pages mentioning httpbin.org/base64 have an indirection-class report in the hour before in 7 of 8 cases.
observations.numbers: Citation (n=1): revision time minus report time = 8270 s. httpbin new mentions n=8 on 8 pages: before-window at 1 h 7/8, Wilson [0.529, 0.978]; shift-null mean 0.5 of 8; after-window 7/8.
observations.mechanical_explanation: n is tiny. There are 4568 indirection reports in total, many of them during the campaign weeks.

observations.skeptic_problem: The sample understates the mismatch rate: the full-population rate 0.9954 lies below the sample's cluster CI [0.997, 1.0]. The 'unverified' explanation is now verified: every mismatch is a harness display format (persisted preview, warning, dedup reference) or dataset redaction. A detector would therefore have to whitelist these formats. 'Holds in cc_local' covers main sessions only; subagent files carry no Read numLines.
observations.skeptic_numbers: Swechat sample matches exactly: 2510/2514 = 0.9984, Wilson [0.9959, 0.9994], cluster [0.9970, 1.0] over 149 files; 4 mismatching files; diffs -2312 to -1. The 4 are 3 persisted-output previews and 1 case with numLines=1 and no numbered text lines (L=0). Full swechat population: 87827/88229 = 0.9954, Wilson [0.9950, 0.9959], cluster [0.9947, 0.9960] over 4603 files; 275 mismatching files; 402 diffs from -3464 to -1, median -1140. All 402 mismatches are harness or dataset formats: 282 '<\persisted-output>' previews, 105 'file shorter than offset' warnings, 7 '<identical to result [rN]...>' references, 7 redacted contents and 1 negative line numbers. None is unexplained. cc_local main sessions, full: 570/578 = 0.986, Wilson [0.973, 0.993], cluster [0.976, 0.994] over 182 files; all 8 mismatches are empty-file warnings with diff -1. In cc_local subagent files, 0 of 12 Read results carry numLines.
observations.statement: In Claude Code logs, the harness's Read counter toolUseResult.file.numLines equals the number of line-numbered lines in the text the model sees. This holds in both swechat and cc_local.
observations.numbers: swechat 2510/2514 = 0.998, Wilson [0.996, 0.999], cluster 0.998 [0.997, 1.0] over 149 files, 4 files mismatch. Mismatch diffs (text minus numLines), n=4: min -2312, median -1595, max -1. cc_local 191/194 = 0.985, Wilson [0.956, 0.995], 59 files, all 3 diffs -1.
observations.mechanical_explanation: Both fields are written by the same harness from the same read, so this is internal redundancy, not an independent witness. The 4 large negative mismatches may be truncated or persisted outputs (unverified).

observations.skeptic_problem: The JSON stores the uncheckable set as I5_cc_agent_toolcount_no_nested_traffic with match 94, n 94, rate 1.0 and a Wilson CI. The code calls add(True), so a non-check is encoded as a 100% pass. It should be a bare count. The statement itself words this correctly. A quarter of Agent results cannot be checked.
observations.skeptic_numbers: Sample matches exactly: 190/190, Wilson [0.980, 1.0], 71 files; 94 results in 20 files have no nested traffic. Full population: 6623/6623, Wilson [0.9994, 1.0], 1934 files. Uncheckable: 2150 results in 634 files, which is 2150/8773 = 0.245 [0.236, 0.254] of Agent/Task results. The uncheckable results have a median totalToolUseCount of 21, so they are not trivially empty.
observations.statement: A subagent's totalToolUseCount (Agent/Task toolUseResult) equals the number of distinct nested tool_use ids in its agent_progress traffic.
observations.numbers: 190/190 = 1.0, Wilson [0.980, 1.0], 71 files. A further 94 results in 20 files have no nested traffic, so they could not be checked.
observations.mechanical_explanation: The harness counts the same stream it writes, so this is redundancy, not independence.

observations.skeptic_problem: 'The IR drops' is false for 3 of the 5 fields. load_swechat.py was saved before the lens ran. At line 707 it sets the OpenCode result ts to state.time.end. At lines 547/560/606/609 it maps Codex exec and MCP durations to extra.duration_s. load_aiv_cu.py line 1095 keeps updated_at in the result's extra field. The lens's own flagged[] marks these paths loader_pair or loader_leaf. Only hookInfos[].durationMs, and info.time.completed outside message-error events, are really dropped. AI Village updated_at is a copy of the row-insert time, not an independent clock.

observations.skeptic_problem: The core claim reproduces within CIs. The out-of-cwd figure 0.049 is conditional on a subset that excludes the 142 sessions whose edits are all outside cwd; over all sessions with edits it is 0.084. 'files_touched is committed files' is only approximate: files_touched ⊄ commit files in 13% of sessions, and 1104 edited paths are in files_touched without being committed. The 'iff committed' hypothesis was introduced in the followup, after the set-equality null. It was declared before its own computation, but it is post hoc relative to the first pass.
observations.skeptic_numbers: I used my own path normalization (in-cwd relative paths), so the n differ. Set equality between in-cwd Write/Edit paths and files_touched (both non-empty): 1719/4346 = 0.396 [0.381, 0.410]. files_touched ⊆ files in the canonical checkpoint's commits: 2780/3196 = 0.870 [0.858, 0.881]. 2x2 over 2828 sessions: in ft & committed 7586; not in ft & not committed 7445; in ft & not committed 1104; not in ft & committed 724. Agreement cluster_rate 0.892 [0.877, 0.905], against about 0.50 expected if the two were independent. Share of files_touched entries that were tool-edited: pooled 0.324 [0.228, 0.444] over 4815 sessions. Out-of-cwd share of edited paths: 0.046 [0.042, 0.050] on the lens's subset (files_touched non-empty and at least 1 in-cwd edit). Over all 4452 sessions with edits it is 0.084 [0.073, 0.095]. 995 of the 2412 out-of-cwd paths are under /.claude/ (plan files), and 142 sessions have only out-of-cwd edits.
observations.statement: files_touched is git-side bookkeeping (committed files), not the set of tool-edited paths. Under a hypothesis declared before computing, an edited path is in files_touched iff it was committed in about 90% of paths.
observations.numbers: Set equality with Write/Edit paths 1628/4276 = 0.381 [0.366, 0.395]. files_touched ⊆ commit files 2812/3201 = 0.878 [0.867, 0.889]. Out-of-cwd edits 0.049 [0.045, 0.053].
observations.mechanical_explanation: The harness derives files_touched from git state at commit. Bash-created and human edits enter it; uncommitted edits do not.

observations.skeptic_problem: The causal reading is not supported. (1) The 'formatter-heavy languages' cause is not shown. The Go excess is one repo (entireio/cli); in other repos Go is 0.066, below average. Whitespace normalization makes gofmt alignment changes invisible. Languages formatted by prettier or black are below average (ts 0.093, tsx 0.085, py 0.098). (2) Half of the worktree calls come from the same repo, and the remaining effect is weak. (3) 'Most contradicted-looking Edits have mechanical causes' is overstated: the only demonstrated mechanism is partial-line edit strings (35% rescued, small decoy inflation). Attribution class, worktree and extension are correlates. (4) The css and kt figures are sample noise. Numbers reproduce in direction; the attribution gradient holds outside entireio/cli (agent_only 0.061, human_only 0.131, mixed 0.238).

observations.skeptic_problem: None in substance. Small point: the lens clusters commit-row data by 'session', which is ill-defined because each row belongs to a checkpoint with several sessions. I clustered by checkpoint.

observations.skeptic_problem: The HTTP Date header has 1 s resolution, so the API response time lies somewhere in [date, date + 1 s). Order is established only where the difference is -1000 ms or less: 2831/3246 flash and 7276/8990 pro. The rest are ambiguous. The direction is expected by construction (the row is inserted after the action runs), and the loader already uses this check. It is a consistency check, not a discovery. The observation has no mechanical_explanation field.
observations.skeptic_numbers: Call rows only: flash 3246/3246 negative (92 sessions), pro 8990/8990 (255 sessions). Medians -4434 / -4574 ms; values closest to zero -78.2 / -111.8 ms. The lens's 3264 / 9028 also count assistant rows of the same turns. 0 http_date values have fractional seconds. Rows with a difference above -1000 ms: 415 flash, 1714 pro.
observations.statement: The Gemini HTTP Date header always precedes the row insert time.
observations.numbers: Negative in 3264/3264 rows (flash) and 9028/9028 (pro). Medians -4.4 s / -4.6 s; the closest values are -78 ms and -112 ms.
observations.mechanical_explanation: The response header is stamped before the action executes and the row is inserted.

observations.skeptic_problem: Counts match to within 1 to 5 results; the lens dedupes results on call_id and I did not. Two refinements. (1) The mechanism is specific to the built-in Bash tool, not to shell commands in general: MCP bash tools behave like non-shell tools. aiv_cc's 0.659 comes from mcp__village__bash, not from partial Bash coverage. (2) The swechat non-shell results are not 'all true': I find 1 false. The tool-conditional coverage strengthens nerr_rate vs shell_share from -0.659 to -0.897. It does not create the correlation by itself.

observations.statement: In Claude Code logs, native_error (is_error) depends on the tool. It is written for essentially every shell result, but for non-shell results only when it is true. Any native_error-based error rate therefore tracks shell share.

observations.statement: In swechat, gap_input_ms (call ts minus latest earlier input ts) is contaminated by interleaving between streams. observations.skeptic_problem: The core hit reproduces, including in the A splits. 'Stable, harness-specific rate' is overstated. The rate depends on the model (Haiku is about 2.4x Opus) and on the predecessor. For call-to-call transitions in the same response, the clock nearly breaks down (cc_local about 1,270 chars/s, within-tool 0.32), consistent with parallel tool_use blocks being written almost together. The usable witness is mainly text/thinking-to-tool_use transitions in main-thread streams. My cc_local within-tool lower CI bound with exact re-ranking is 0.499, against the lens's 0.707.

observations.statement: Block streaming clock: for a tool_use whose previous event is a block of the same API response, the timestamp gap tracks the length of its arguments at a stable, harness-specific rate. This holds in three Claude-Code-family corpora and in their held-out A splits.

observations.mechanical_explanation: Each content block is timestamped when it finishes streaming, so the gap is the generation time of the block (serving physics). This is the call-level counterpart of the aiv_accounting block-gap result.

observations.skeptic_problem: The numbers reproduce, but 'Not mechanical' is wrong. Most of the clustering comes from harness cascades over parallel calls in one response: a failed sibling cancels the rest, a user interrupt rejects all pending calls, and a permission denial is repeated. That also explains why the effect is strongest in Claude Code logs. After the controls, swechat CC keeps a small cross-response effect (0.041, above its null). cc_local's CI includes 0 and aiv_cc is about 0. The proposed error-burst witness would mostly detect harness cascade structure.
observations.skeptic_numbers: Within-session lag-1 rho of err (null counted as no error), against 20 within-session permutations. swechat 0.183 [0.158, 0.206] vs -0.009. swechat CC 0.197 vs -0.008. cc_local 0.129 [0.088, 0.297] vs -0.011. aiv_cc 0.052 [0.010, 0.117] vs 0.001. Codex 0.057. OpenCode 0.044. Who&When (non-null err) -0.483 vs a null of -0.382. Mechanical controls: (1) Drop CC sibling-cancellation results ('Cancelled: parallel tool call', 1,214) and interrupt results (662), which together are 23% of the 8,141 CC errors. swechat CC falls to 0.076. (2) Also keep only pairs from different API responses: swechat CC 0.041 [0.031, 0.051] (null -0.008), cc_local 0.057 [-0.018, 0.093], aiv_cc 0.010, OpenCode -0.052 (null -0.013). In cc_local, 132 of the 136 same-response error pairs are permission-denied cascades. Shell only, controls applied: swechat CC 0.086.
observations.statement: Errors cluster within sessions beyond what session-level error-rate differences explain. The effect is strongest in Claude Code logs, small in OpenCode and Codex, and absent in Who&When.

observations.mechanical_explanation: Not mechanical. The permutation null removes the composition and short-series bias. Plausible cause (untested): retry loops after a failure.

observations.skeptic_problem: The coupling survives within session (not just session composition), and a residual of about 0.15 to 0.16 remains in single-call last-block responses in all three CC-family corpora. 'No mechanism' is partly overstated. In cc_local most of it runs through arg_len (partial 0.083). In multi-call responses, sibling-result interleaving (see O11) inflates it. The three replicating corpora share one harness family, and the pair is absent where the loader stamps lat as execution start to end (OpenCode). That points to the non-execution part of CC's lat (untested).

observations.skeptic_problem: 'The shorter turnaround is unexplained' is mostly refuted. The call-level effect is a gap_input artifact. Claude Code writes sibling results before later sibling calls, so the later calls' 'turnaround' is measured from a sibling result. Per response, fan-out responses are only slightly faster to start (-0.13), which fits their smaller context, and they take the same total time (-0.01).

Input to the response's last block vs resp_ncalls: -0.010 and -0.009. resp_turn vs resp_ctx: 0.32 and 0.31.
observations.statement: Fan-out structure (Claude Code family only): responses that issue several calls have smaller context, shorter args and much shorter turnaround. They do not have less thinking, so less thinking does not explain the shorter turnaround.

observations.skeptic_problem: None for the numbers; they agree within Monte Carlo error. The mechanism holds: sd(diff)/sqrt(2) = sigma*sqrt(1-rho). observations.statement: Detector calibration: binary segmentation with a BIC-style penalty keeps a false-positive rate of 0.013-0.05 on i.i.d. data, but it is badly over-sensitive under AR(1) dependence. The observed series sit in that range: swechat latency median lag-1 is 0.354 and result_len 0.220. The block-shuffle control (10-point blocks) is the honest yardstick.
observations.mechanical_explanation: Gaussian mean-shift with sigma estimated from first differences underestimates the marginal sd under positive autocorrelation, so persistence reads as level shifts.

observations.skeptic_problem: The co-occurrence numbers reproduce, but the mechanism is mis-stated. In Claude Code a switch-induced cache miss shows up as cache_creation up and cache_read down. usage_in moves by a few tokens (median 1 -> 9), so the usage_in CP is a log1p shift of tiny counts, not a 'jump in uncached input'. Returning to a recently used model often hits its cache (52%). The thinking couplings rest on 5-9 events.

observations.skeptic_problem: The numbers reproduce, but three caveats apply. (1) 0.999 counts any earlier read, not the same file, so a single read at the start of a stream passes every later edit. It is not evidence of the gate; the refusal contrast is. (2) The gate is per agent: a read done in a subagent does not unlock an edit in main (36/44 refused). The gate also leaks in the log: 187 edits with no visible read or write still succeed, and compaction probably resets read state (39/128, mechanism UNVERIFIED). (3) 'OpenCode shows the same order' overclaims. Its same-path strict rate is 0.66-0.82 depending on path matching, against 0.96 for CC. Its edits are mostly apply_patch, and file-creating patches sit in the denominator. It has no gate, so the comparison is not like for like.

observations.skeptic_problem: The direction (several-fold shrink) reproduces, but the headline values do not hold at FPR 1%. The lens's swechat edit/grep values (1122) are about 1.5-1.8x smaller than mine. Part of the cause is that eff_rate scales tokens/char by the newline and non-ASCII density of the existing result, which raises the rate for short results such as edit snippets.

Share of exceedances: at the q99 threshold 102 of 1425 (0.072); for |r| > 10000, 57 of 138 (0.413); for |r| > 20000, 47 of 71 (0.662). dC < 0: 72 of 95.
observations.statement: A cache miss leaves C unchanged in the typical case, but pairs with a cache-read drop carry most unlogged context edits.

observations.mechanical_explanation: C sums input + cache_read + cache_create, so a TTL miss only moves tokens between fields. A context rewrite without a logged marker both invalidates the cache and changes C.

observations.skeptic_problem: The headline n=154,815 quietly adds 50 Vertex ids that the loader stored in api_msg_id (Vertex writes a req_vrtx_ value as the message id). That is a parser surprise and should be stated. 'Biased bits exactly at 62, 63, 75-79' depends on the lens's |p-0.5|>0.05 rule. A significance rule also flags cc_local bits 66 and 67 (z about -6.4 and -7.8). Bit 75 is not always 0 in cc_local (2.0%). The layout is supported by the data but stays UNVERIFIED.

Biased bits in swechat are 62, 63 and 75-79, with P(bit75)=0.000. In cc_local P(bit75)=0.020, and bits 66 and 67 have P=0.482 and 0.478 (z=-6.4 and -7.8). Scripts: scratchpad/rd/o1.py, o1b.py.
observations.statement: Anthropic request ids are RFC 9562 UUIDv7 values encoded in base58 after 'req_01'. Every one carries version 7 and variant 2, and V >> 80 is unix ms. Newer message ids have the same layout.
observations.numbers: v7|var2: swechat req 154,815/154,815 (2,418.98 expected by chance); cc_local req 31,085/31,085; cc_local msg 30,680/30,680; aiv_cu msg time-format 8,232/8,240. Biased bits sit exactly at 62, 63 and 75-79.
observations.mechanical_explanation: The vendor mints request and message ids as UUIDv7 and renders them as base58 behind a '01' version prefix. The layout was inferred from the data and is UNVERIFIED against documentation.
