candidate_mechanisms.name: Unread-clock stamp detector: an agent-emitted epoch that is later than an external record of the save carrying it
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: For every epoch-like token an agent writes (page name, prose, not inside URLs), compute delta = token - the server's save time. Flag delta > +1 s; the server reports 1 s uncertainty, and real-clock reads show median -1 s with 0/459 fraction-form stamps after the save. The round-number feature is a prior, not the test. Validate on a holdout corpus where the agent's tool calls are known.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Server-generated expiry tokens and incrementing ID sequences inside URLs; IDs that happen to look like epochs; deliberately future-dated markers; container clock skew (small here, median -1 to -2 s).
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: the idea of detecting LLM 'now' guesses by comparing them against an independent server clock seems uncommon. Clock-skew forensics exist in general.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Source-level cross-witness corroboration: an independent URL-scan service records activity on the same data source within the hour before the agent writes about it
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: For each first mention of source S, test for >=1 scan report for S in [t-1h, t) against local shifted nulls (+-2h/4h/1d) and a source-permutation null; report the excess with page-clustered CIs. Use it only to corroborate (raise confidence when present), never to accuse when a report is missing.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Same-campaign co-activity by other agents or operators; scan catalogs whose query choice was informed by the wiki; sources the scanner rarely covers (DataUSA 0.038, Census 0/58), where absence carries no information.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: using a third-party URL scanner's public report timestamps as a witness for agent tool use seems novel. The general idea of corroborating logs across independent systems is not.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Narrated wall-clock residual: an agent's own 'current UTC' statement compared with the server save time
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Real-clock-qualified times compared with the save time: the median residual (-84 s) and the asymmetry within the +-1h fold (601 vs 95) show the agent read a clock. Present- or past-tense claims later than the save are candidate impossibilities, but at this resolution the near-future rate (0.056) does not beat the unrelated-clock control (0.067).
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Projections phrased in the present tense; times of day with no date that fold across midnight; task-clock times sitting next to a 'UTC' keyword; approximate values ('~').
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: probably not novel as a forensic idea. It needs a dated claim format or hand labels before it can flag individual claims.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Storage-order vs timestamp-order inversion (RCS commit number vs time)
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Per page, adjacent RCS revisions whose timestamps go backwards. Observed 72/10012 on 4 pages, all 1-5 s.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Concurrent writers on hot pages (timestamp taken before the commit lock). Every inversion observed here fits a race, so this mainly documents a false-positive source for any order-based consistency check.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: standard concurrency forensics; not novel.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Structured-counter vs visible-text recount
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: For each tool result, recount the quantity from the model-visible text or the call arguments and compare it to the harness counter by exact equality, pre-registered. Honest baseline I4: 2510/2514 (swechat) and 191/194 (cc_local). Rewritten or fabricated result text should break the equality unless the counter is rewritten too.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Truncated or persisted-to-file outputs, system reminders appended to result text, line-number formatting changes across harness versions, and Read calls with an offset or limit.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: I don't know of published work that uses the harness's structured copy of a tool result as a cross-check. Agent-observability tools may do this already.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Second-clock duration consistency
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Check that each harness timer is at most the gap between the surrounding event clocks (call to end, turn start to end), with a tolerance set from an honest baseline before any outcome is examined. A reported duration longer than the wall-clock gap, or a gap with no possible execution time, would flag a result that was not produced by execution.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Parallel tool calls, clocks written at flush time rather than event time, millisecond granularity, skew between processes, and backgrounded commands.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: duration-vs-timestamp checks are standard in log forensics. Applying them to agent tool logs may be less common.

candidate_mechanisms.name: file-history-snapshot mutation reconciliation
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: For each successful Edit or Write on path P at time t, expect a later snapshot to show a version bump for P with backupTime >= t. Count claimed edits that have no bump, and bumps that have no claimed edit.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Snapshots are per user message, so edits coalesce. Paths outside the tracked set are missing. About 19% of files have no snapshot at all. Resumed sessions and Bash-made edits also break the mapping.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: this harness record seems unused in the literature I know of.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Session-tally recount
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Recompute each tally from the transcript (usage sums, tool counts, patch line sums) and compare. Report the disagreement rate with a session-clustered CI.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Tallies derived from the same transcript agree tautologically. Resumed or compacted sessions change the totals. Subagent tokens may be included in one count and not the other.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED

candidate_mechanisms.name: Cumulative counter chain
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Check the chain identity total(n) = total(n-1) + last(n), and that ordinal counters only increase. Honest baseline I1b: 0.970, with breaks in 5/26 files.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Counter resets at compaction, rollback or resume, which plausibly explain the observed breaks (unverified).
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED

candidate_mechanisms.name: Nested-subagent tally check
grounded_in: CC toolUseResult.totalToolUseCount / totalTokens / totalDurationMs (captured in extra)
cc_local workflow.json totalToolCalls vs subagent JSONL
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Compare the parent's reported subagent tallies with a recount of the nested or sidecar subagent transcript. Baseline I5: 190/190.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Nesting is absent in current Claude Code (cc_local), and subagent files can be missing or truncated.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED

candidate_mechanisms.name: External git witness of claimed edits
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Match the agent-claimed patch hunks to the committed diff, and report the fraction of claimed hunks that never reach a commit.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Human edits between agent and commit, squashed or rebased commits, and work that was never committed. Another lens (phase_c_commit_witness) may already cover this.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED

candidate_mechanisms.name: AI Village dual record of model calls
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Join an event to its turn and compare usage and the action between the two tables.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Events exist only for some action types, the join key is uncertain, and created_at is a row-insert time that can lag the event.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED

candidate_mechanisms.name: Out-of-band usage-ledger reconciliation
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Recompute (count of distinct API message ids, summed last-occurrence usage) from the transcript and require an exact 5-field match with a tally the harness wrote outside the transcript at commit time. Allow prefix and declared-offset windows. Honest floor: 33/5701 = 0.0058 [0.0041, 0.0081] unexplained after correcting the join artifact.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Snapshots taken mid-stream (output-only mismatch, 7 of 14 Claude residuals), dev/old CLI builds, multi-checkpoint snapshot mixing in derived tables, OpenCode/Gemini messages whose token fields change after the snapshot. Blind to edits of tool-result content, since usage numbers do not change when a result is altered.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: using a harness-written token ledger as a witness-free check on transcript integrity (inserted, deleted or duplicated assistant turns) seems uncommon. Usage-based billing reconciliation is standard practice, but not as a transcript-integrity signal.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Provider cache-granularity plausibility check
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Every reported cached-input count must be a multiple of the provider's cache block. On the Codex/OpenAI path: 181/181 multiples of 128. OpenCode 569/619.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Providers or proxies with different block sizes, cumulative counters mixing providers (OpenCode through several providers), and Anthropic usage, which shows no granularity (49/4785 divisible by 128).
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: a stateless arithmetic check on fabricated usage numbers. Likely known to billing engineers, but I have not seen it used for log verification.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Cross-snapshot inconsistency via ratio outliers
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Robust z (|z|>3.5 on ≥3 of 22 features) including ratio features (output/API call, tools/API call, seconds/API call). Rows assembled from two different snapshots are outliers at 9/36 = 0.250 [0.138, 0.411], against 59/4771 = 0.0124 [0.0096, 0.0159] for consistent rows.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Genuinely unusual sessions (very long, many prompts, automation), missing tallies encoded as 0, and early/dev harness builds. Recall is only about 25%.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: a generic data-quality technique. Applied to agent-log rows built from mixed sources, it may be new only in this setting.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Commit-claim window check
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: For each Bash result printing '[branch sha] subject', look up the SHA prefix among the repo's commits. Require commit_date within [call ts - 2 s, result ts + 2 s], plus subject and branch equality. Honest pass rate among resolvable claims is 0.993 (window) and 0.996 (subject), but only 0.624 of claims resolve. A fabricated output would fail to resolve, or resolve outside the window.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: History rewrites (amend/rebase/squash: 356 of the unmatched), commit_not_found checkpoints (303), unpushed commits, commands that re-print earlier commits. 266 of 2178 claims are unmatched with no flag. 9 resolved claims fall outside the window for unknown reasons.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Conceptually close to software provenance/attestation (in-toto/SLSA). Applying it to agent transcripts may be less common; no literature search was done.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Edit-to-commit line corroboration with decoy calibration
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Take the lines each Edit adds (new_string minus old_string, informative lines of 8+ characters, superseded lines removed). Look them up in the target commit's '+' lines and in the committed file content. Honest full match is 0.830 vs 0.003 for the decoy. The per-call 'contradicted' floor is 0.138, or 0.093 after the post-hoc edge-substring rule. That floor is too high for per-call alarms, so the check needs session-level aggregation and conditioning (agent_only target, no worktree, no formatter ecosystem). It covers about 0.532 of the CC mutation stream.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Partial-line edit strings, worktree path matching, hook or editor formatters (go/rs stay at 0.161/0.181), human edits between turns (mixed 0.269), other sessions in the same checkpoint. The residual is 53 calls in 31 sessions with no ground truth.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Diff-based attribution exists (SWE-chat itself attributes code to agent vs human). Using git as a falsifier of tool-result success claims, with a decoy-calibrated chance rate, may be less explored.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Write full-content check against the committed file
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Check whether all informative lines of a Write's content appear in the committed file (file_attribution committed_version) at the first later commit. Honest full match is 0.836 vs a decoy full rate of 0.002; contradicted-looking is 1/2320. Only 'full' is informative, because decoy partial is 0.350.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Later agent or human edits before the commit (the 0.164 partial cases). Files never committed (Write constrained share 0.684).
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Likely an obvious check, so probably not novel.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Harness-record vs transcript key trace (log integrity)
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Hash (path, old_string, new_string) or (path, content) for each agent_changes entry and each transcript Edit/Write call, then match them. 0.856 of entries trace to a listed session. 452 entries appear in no released transcript (60 sessions). This detects transcript loss or truncation, but it cannot detect fabrication, because both records come from the same agent log.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Incomplete checkpoint session lists (4572 entries owned by other same-repo sessions), fork or mirror duplication (3738 entries from same-name repos under other owners), unreleased sessions.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Unexplained committed hunks (reverse check)
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Find committed '+' lines in agent-attributed files that no Edit/Write/Bash text from the linked sessions, or from the owners of the commit's agent_changes, could have produced. This is 0.050 of agent_only lines, with 95 of 8129 files having zero explained lines. It could reveal mutations that were never logged.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Code generated by Bash scripts or codegen, formatters, unparsed tools (NotebookEdit, non-CC scaffolds), linkage gaps (the listed-session-only version gives 0.167), unreliable attribution labels.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Per-turn token conservation (context-delta witness)
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: For consecutive API responses, compare the server-side context delta (input + cache_read + cache_creation) with chars logged in between (previous output, thinking and tool results) using a chars->tokens model fit per corpus. Flag turns with large residuals. Baseline: |residual| median 49.6 tokens, p99 685.7 (hold-out 51.7 / 667.7), n=59804 clean pairs in 190 runs. Each stripped image adds about 899 tokens.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Unlogged context edits (30 resets to the prefix), per-tool framing offsets (-92.7 to -193.8 tokens for 6 built-in tools), images, compaction and resumes. A crude chars model without a tokenizer. Length-preserving substitutions cannot be detected.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: Possibly novel as a fabrication detector for agent tool logs (UNVERIFIED).

candidate_mechanisms.name: Cache-chain continuity check
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Test cache_read(k+1) == cache_read(k) + cache_creation(k) exactly. It holds in 0.99905 of clean pairs (CI 0.99858-0.99943). A break locates where the server saw a history different from a pure append.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Idle gaps of 300 s or more (8/32 break), image handling (203/4570 break), compaction, client-side pruning, resumes (only 1/234 hold).
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: Possibly novel (UNVERIFIED).

candidate_mechanisms.name: Log-vs-ledger reconciliation
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Check the result row against the logged stream: num_turns == user rows + 1 (210/211); result.usage == sum of per-response usage (196/211, never above the sum); modelUsage[main] == result.usage + compaction hidden calls (125/125 without compaction; input 64/65 with it); cost linear in tokens (503/503 model rows). An inserted or deleted turn or tool-result row breaks one of these.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: SDK responses missing from the ledger (12 runs below the sum plus 3 all-zero runs out of 211), associated with a non-null stop_reason. Failed-resume result rows. Hidden auxiliary-model calls (172/211 runs).
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: Ledger reconciliation is a standard audit idea; applying it to agent SDK result rows is probably uncommon (UNVERIFIED).

candidate_mechanisms.name: Hidden-call check of compaction summaries
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Per run, check (modelUsage[main].output - result.usage.output) against the chars of the logged compaction summary. Spearman 0.9975 (CI 0.9912-0.9993), per-run 3.431-4.305 chars/token, n=65 runs.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Only run-level (no per-compaction split when there are several). The token rate differs from tool-content rates.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: Possibly novel (UNVERIFIED).

candidate_mechanisms.name: Generation-rate and wall-clock timing consistency
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: The gap before each block should scale with its chars (Pearson 0.930; median 162.1 chars/s). duration_ms should equal the created_at span (|diff| median 30.1 ms). The created_at call->result gap should be at least the tool-reported duration (28/29, 132/133, 45/47). Rows written in a batch after the fact or fabricated would show floor-level gaps or a mismatched span.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Insert jitter (min slack -37.2 ms), streaming tool execution (3002 results before the calling response's last row), rare long stalls (r031). Applies only to sources with row-insert or event timestamps.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: Timing checks are standard; using streaming block gaps against content size may be less common (UNVERIFIED).

candidate_mechanisms.name: Provider usage-lattice plausibility check
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Check reported prompt image tokens: they must be a sum of per-image costs (Gemini 1064/258). Check cache_read: it must be a multiple of the provider block (Codex 128). Honest on-lattice rate: 10499/10569 (pro), 3219/3219 (flash), Codex cache 1.0.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Off-lattice honest rows (70/10569 on pro). Model or version changes in per-image cost. Cached image tokens are never on the lattice, so only prompt-side counts can be checked.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED; possibly undescribed for agent-log fabrication detection. Not checked against the literature.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Harness-conformance fingerprint (cadence, templates, caps, uncached-input constant)
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Check four things: bash_progress gaps sit at 1000-1004 ms (0.877 of honest gaps); exact template strings and lengths; tool output never exceeds the harness cap (CC 30000 / ~10050 on failure; OpenCode 51551); usage_in equals the harness constant (1, 2, or 8/10).
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Scheduling jitter (only 0.877 of ticks on cadence). Template and cap changes across versions. Failure max 10050 vs a pile at 10039/10040. This tests log provenance, not the truth of tool results.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED; resembles generic log-format validation.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Strict server-clock ordering (Gemini HTTP Date < row insert)
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Test date header < created_at on every Gemini row. It holds in 12292/12292 rows, with a minimum margin of 78 ms.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Clock skew between the server and the DB host. The header has 1 s resolution, so it catches only gross time edits.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED; standard timestamp-consistency auditing.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Reasoning-token lattice as a model fingerprint (session/corpus level)
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: A log claiming gpt-5.4 should show about 0.020 [0.016, 0.028] of token_count rows at 516 + 518k, with empty neighbours.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Unknown mechanism, so it may change with provider updates. The share is low, so the test has no per-row power.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED; the lattice itself may be undocumented.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Block streaming clock as a content-length witness
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: For a tool_use block that follows a block of the same API response, the timestamp gap should match args length divided by the session's own streaming rate. Measured honest-baseline rho: 0.815 / 0.919 / 0.815 pooled and 0.579 / 0.863 / 0.709 within tool, at 175 / 197 / 102 chars/s (swechat CC / cc_local / aiv_cc). A rewritten argument of different length would break the rate.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: The rate differs by model and harness (102 vs 175 chars/s). Only 0.31-0.40 of CC calls have a same-response predecessor (0.96 in aiv_cc). Within-tool rho is lower (0.58 in swechat). Stalls and retries inflate gaps. aiv_cu (one stamp per turn), OpenCode and Codex lack the block structure.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Possibly not described for agent-log verification. aiv_accounting reported the block-level version for aiv_cc, and I did not search the literature.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Turnaround vs generated volume (one-sided latency bound)
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: gap_input_ms should be at least the time implied by logged output tokens, thinking chars and context. Within-tool rho: 0.356 (swechat, resp_out), 0.551 (aiv_cc, resp_think), 0.401 (aiv_cu, resp_out). Gemini server timing vs reasoning chars: 0.517.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Placeholder usage_out (F2: 0.865 in aiv_cc, 0.782 on swechat subagent copies). Cross-stream ordering in swechat and parallel-call ordering in OpenCode (F7). Haiku subagents running faster (F6). Human or permission waits that only lengthen gaps. So it works as a one-sided bound, not as an equality.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Latency proportional to tokens is common knowledge. Using it as a log-consistency bound may or may not have been described.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Error-burst statistic (lag-1 error autocorrelation vs permutation null)
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Within-session lag-1 correlation of the error flag, compared with within-session permutations. Honest CC-family logs: 0.129-0.197 against a null of about -0.01. aiv_cc 0.052; Codex 0.056; OpenCode 0.044. A log with independently injected or scrubbed errors would sit at the null.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Short sessions bias the statistic negative (Who&When). The effect is small in OpenCode and Codex. native_error coverage depends on the tool (F1), so the error flag must combine native_error with text markers. It is a session-level test that needs many calls.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Error clustering in agent traces is probably known behaviorally. Its use as a fabrication statistic was not checked.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Turnaround-latency coupling
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Within tool, slow model turns predict slow tool execution: 0.18-0.23 in swechat, aiv_cc and cc_local; 5/5 independent replications; stream-aware 0.214-0.234. A log assembled from independently drawn latencies would lack it.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: The mechanism is unknown, so the false-positive structure is unknown. Absent in OpenCode and Codex. A small effect that needs many calls per session.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. The weakest of the four. I have no mechanism and did not check the literature.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Context-drop accounting
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Every sharp drop in server-reported context size (usage_in + cache_read + cache_create) must sit within a few events of a logged compaction, /clear or harness-synthetic message. On honest data, after the post-hoc synthetic and edge rules, the residue is 0/350 swechat and 0/492 aiv_cc ctx down-shifts. It is 4/8 in aiv_cu, where compaction is not logged.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Harness channels that do not log compaction (aiv_cu); '<synthetic>' zero-usage rows; detector boundary pinning. It is blind to length-preserving edits and overlaps with the aiv_accounting cache-chain check.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED; likely a variant of token-conservation checks already seen in aiv_accounting.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Model-switch cache-miss signature
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: A logged model switch should coincide with a jump in uncached input, because prompt caches are per model. Measured here only as change-point co-occurrence (usage_in x model_switch tight o/e 12.6 [7.7, 21.8]); per-switch identity rates were not measured.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Cache expiry or invalidation without a switch (compaction, task notifications also enrich usage_in shifts); Haiku interleaving of unknown cause.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED; no literature check.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Thinking-time coupling
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Regime shifts in thinking volume co-occur with shifts in inter-call gap (aiv_cc o/e 21.3 [14.9, 34.5], swechat 2.83). A log claiming heavy reasoning at short gaps, or the reverse, would break a coupling seen on honest data. The per-event relation was not measured.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Redacted or empty thinking (thinking is constant in 355/970 swechat sessions); provider latency variation; parallel calls.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Harness timeout-ceiling timing witness
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: For each tool family, look at the call->result gap distribution in 2 s bins. Within a scaffold, the honest log shows spikes at fixed ceilings: [120,122) s for shell, [600,602) s for TaskOutput and shell. Flag any logged call whose gap exceeds the ceiling without a timeout marker, and any timeout-style result whose gap is not at the ceiling. Measured spikes: swechat 235 gaps at 120 s vs 56/74 in the neighbouring bins, and 173 at 600 s vs 0/8. cc_local 117 vs 3/3 and 75 vs 2/1.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Human approval waits create long gaps that are not tool runtime (O11, cc_interrupt_reject after 16829.7 s). Per-call timeout overrides and different scaffold timeouts also produce gaps. Gaps cluster in few sessions (swechat 600 s bin: 23 sessions), so rates need session-clustered CIs (not computed). aiv_cu shared_turn stamps carry no gap at all.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: using fixed harness timeout ceilings as a timing witness for agent tool logs may not be described; timing checks in general are standard.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Within-stratum template-deviation score with a permutation-calibrated tail cut
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Compute robust z on about 30-39 IR session features within scaffold/stratum, not pooled. Choose the axis-count cut k where the observed count exceeds the column-permutation null: k>=5-8, for example swechat >=5 182 vs 60.1 and aiv_cu >=8 46 vs 0.5. At k>=3 the count is at or below the null. Report sessions above k as candidates.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Several sources of honest outliers: dominant templates and harness caps (cc_local 92/186 template; aiv_cu 35684/78114 at 41 turns), tiny sessions with degenerate shares (aiv_cu picks 9/10 with <=10 events), and loader unit artifacts (aiv_cc failed-resume rows). The co-movement is partly built in by construction. This cut was not pre-registered and was not applied.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: multi-feature robust anomaly scoring is standard; applying it to agent tool logs with a permutation-calibrated axis count is probably not new as a method.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Provider-listed vs executed call consistency
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: For each logged provider response, compare the calls the provider listed with the calls the harness executed. The executed set must be a subset of the listed set, and dropped calls must follow the harness's one-action-per-turn rule. Measured: gemini-pro has 39 sessions extreme on unexecuted_calls; pick 6 has 20 unexecuted calls vs 19 executed.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Silent drops are normal harness behaviour for multi-call Gemini responses. Call-id fallbacks (gemini-pro 224 sessions) weaken the call matching.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: checking provider-emitted call lists against executed actions as a log-integrity witness may not be described.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Harness-gate grammar check
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Per stream, verify the harness-enforced orderings: Read(path) before Edit(path), with a refusal followed by Read and an identical retry; TaskCreate before TaskUpdate; ToolSearch before deferred tools. Honest conformance: 28768/28802 CC edits have an earlier read when both tools are present; 197/205 refusal-retries pass through a same-path Read.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Same-path strictness (1143/28808 CC edits have no same-path read in the stream, possibly context from resumed or compacted history); version drift (cc_local strict 231/1457 with 0 refusals); scaffolds without the gate (Codex has no read tool, Gemini).
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Treating harness-enforced tool preconditions as an integrity grammar for logs may be unexplored, but process-mining conformance checking is close prior art.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Tool-vocabulary version/configuration fingerprint
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Check that the tool set and per-tool usage grammar match the claimed harness version or model: TodoWrite vs Task* mutual exclusion (27/4749, 2/1310); per-model get_pixel_coords-before-click rates (0.00 for Claude vs 0.82-0.92 for Gemini/o3/gpt-5.2); cd-prefix and PowerShell style per scaffold.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Sessions resumed across harness upgrades; agent-specific tool provisioning (model = agent = period confound in aiv_cu); small n for many models.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Behavioural fingerprinting of agents/models from action sequences probably exists in some form.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Outcome-conditioned repetition test
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Compare exact or near-identical re-issue rates after 'ok' vs 'fail' results with a corpus baseline. In CC an exact repeat after ok is 0.008 vs 0.131 after fail, so a repeat following an 'ok' result flags a result whose true outcome may differ (or a flaky tool).
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Polling and GUI corpora where identical repeats are routine (aiv_cc exact-after-ok 0.391, aiv_cu retry-after-ok 0.303); flaky tools; subagent retries (0/77 exact).
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Using the agent's own reaction to a result as an implicit witness of that result's outcome may be new.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Unverified-completion prior
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Per mutation stream, check whether any test or build call follows the last mutation (CC 0.363 verify, 0.216 test). Pair this with end-of-session success claims; the claims are not measured in this lens.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Tasks without tests; verification by hooks or CI outside the log; regex misses for test commands.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Likely covered informally by claim-checking work.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Failure-position prior for blame localisation
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Rank candidate mistake steps by proximity to failed executions (21/41 vs 11.429 expected under the uniform null in Who&When AG).
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Half of annotated mistakes are not at failure steps; HC has no failure markers.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Probably overlaps with Who&When baselines.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Matched-narration grounding test (self-report vs own tool log with an other-agent null)
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: For each checkable entity in the narration (path, filename, command, hex id, printed number, URL, quoted text), test whether it appears in the session's call args or result text. Compare that support rate with the support of a same-time narration from a different agent against the same log. Flag sessions where own support falls to the other-agent baseline. STOP baseline: path 0.048, quoted 0.047; own: 0.622 / 0.331.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: GUI-heavy sessions where facts came from screenshots (support falls to 0.288 for gui_gt_half); memory carry-over of claims about earlier sessions (0.262-0.384 of claims); claims about other agents' work; placeholder summaries; forward-looking plan text.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: using a matched other-agent narration as the chance baseline for self-report vs log checks may not be described for agent-log verification. Literature not checked.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Assertion-conditioned action evidence (asserted push/commit/PR must have a matching call)
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Per action, compare P(log has an evidence call | narration asserts it) with P(same | no mention). For a single session, flag an asserted action that has no evidence call while the shell channel was in use. STOP push: 0.633 vs 0.153.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Third-party and earlier-session attributions and planned command blocks (contradicted_absent is 0.29 for own narration vs 0.45 for unrelated narration, so a raw absence rule has no specificity); actions done through the GUI; low recall (0.18-0.42), so a missing claim is uninformative.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: likely close to existing claim-vs-trace consistency checks; the low-specificity finding in multi-agent settings may be the new part.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Plan-to-execution chain check (previous nextSessionGoal = next session's goal; check follow-through)
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Use the exact chain (1,470 equal vs 3 differ) to check whether commands, paths and hashes named in the previous narration appear in the next session's log. Goal command support is 0.479, while the narration written after the session supports its own commands at only 0.355 (diff -0.092).
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Legitimate plan changes; long forward plans that cover several sessions; state recaps mixed into the goal text.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: cross-session plan-vs-trace checking may not be described for this data; literature not checked.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Narration provenance gap detector (summary not produced by any logged call)
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Test whether the narration text appears in any logged model output, and whether its length fits the logged output tokens. Here: 0/25,939 summaries in the STOP output; chars > 8x outputTokens in 0.801 of rows; length tracks the post-session delay (Spearman 0.416).
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Harness-generated summaries are benign by design in this dataset, so the gap is structural, not adversarial. The check only says the narration cannot be tied to a logged generation.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: a generic provenance/accounting idea; probably not novel.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Cross-field timer identities as per-record checksums
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Recompute each redundant timer from the stamps it duplicates and require equality within a few ms. Pairs: Stop-hook summary = first hook start + max duration; mcp elapsed = completed - started; Agent totalDurationMs = result - first nested; OpenCode id ms = created; Codex wall time = exec duration - ~102 ms. Honest floor: 0 violations at 2 ms in thousands of records (0/6714, 0/1147, 1900/2188 within 2 ms, 208/208, 2357/2357 within [-139,-50] ms).
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Bulk re-stamped history (Claude Code 1.0.x gap-0 169/2327) breaks the stamp side. Clock glitches move both fields together and are absorbed (slack +9 ms on the -2.3 s glitch). Subagent ticks reported under the parent id (8879 events) must be routed separately.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: using harness-internal duplicate timer encodings as tamper checksums for agent tool logs may be uncommon; not checked against literature.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Third-party clock bracketing (model API timing headers)
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: For each model turn, the provider's server-timing duration must fit inside the logger's inter-row gap, and the row must not precede the provider's HTTP Date. 0/12292 violations; min slack 564 ms (gap) and 78 ms (Date).
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Only providers that return timing headers (Gemini here; none in the Anthropic/OpenAI aiv_cu shapes). First rows of a session have no prior anchor. Very long gaps (max ~72e6 ms) make the bound loose rather than wrong.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: cross-checking agent-log timestamps against provider HTTP/server-timing headers as an external witness may not be described for fabrication detection.

candidate_mechanisms.name: 1 Hz progress-tick chain with per-call phase lock
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Ticks of one Bash call satisfy lag >= 1000*elapsed (0/112677), advance by 1 s (delta 1 in 106390 pairs), and keep a constant sub-second phase (per-call range median 6 ms). The first tick yields a per-call execution-start estimate (pre-exec delay median 73 ms, p95 28 s). Inserted, deleted or shifted results or ticks break the chain.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Machine suspend (tick gaps with wall-clock elapsed jumps; 1 timeout overrun, 377/378 gaps wall-consistent). Subagent Bash ticks under Task/Agent parent ids. Not available in cc_local or aiv_cc (no progress stream).
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: progress-heartbeat phase consistency as an integrity signal for agent logs is a guess at novelty.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Harness-constant fingerprints
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Plausibility rules recovered from honest data: retryInMs band 500*2^(a-1)*[1,1.25] capped (533/533); Codex 30 s yield cap (0/1682 after cap); Claude Code 600000 ms Bash timeout clamp (9/9 mismatches); cc_local 900 s exit after last event (66/70); first tick at elapsed 2 or 3; Codex ~102 ms wall/duration offset. A log not emitted by the harness must reproduce all of them.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Constants are version- and launch-mode-specific (only measured in the B samples). Clamps make argument values differ from effective timers, so an argument-vs-observed mismatch is not evidence.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: likely related to generic software fingerprinting; specific use on agent logs not checked.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Embedded-identifier clocks (UUIDv7 / OpenCode ascending ids)
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Decode creation ms from ids and require id ms <= the announcing event ts (Codex 0/360, 0/77, 0/56; OpenCode assistant parts 0 violations, session ids within 1 ms). A copied or invented id inconsistent with its event time stands out.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Client-minted user-side ids precede server stamps (267/518, median -6.5 ms, min -13.5 s). Redacted ids are undecodable (3545 of 26792 OpenCode parts not decodable).
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: time-ordered ids are well known; using them as a second clock against logged timestamps for agent-log verification is an unverified guess.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Timestamp-degeneracy screen (abstention rule)
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Flag sessions with tie runs >=5 identically stamped entries or call->result gaps exactly 0. Timing-based detectors must abstain there (1.0.x gap-0 169/2327 vs 2.1.x 329/133590; 10 runs >=20 events, max 68).
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Fast tools can legitimately share a millisecond in 2.1.x (329 pairs). Transient backward reads produce negative gaps that are not tampering.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: a prerequisite rather than a detector; novelty not claimed.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Per-call context-delta conservation check with tool-aware thresholds
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Out-of-fold residual of dC against logged window content (M_hyb). Thresholds come from the other fold's honest residuals, per tool type. Min detectable single-result change: swechat CC edit / shell 1122-1259 chars at power 0.5; aiv_cc gui 282 chars; pooled 5623-8913 chars.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Hidden-content tools (ToolSearch exceed 0.198, ExitPlanMode 0.185, Skill, TaskOutput), compaction, microcompaction, images, human-turn thinking stripping, cache-miss-coincident context edits (exceed 0.163), Codex truncation above about 40-60k chars, streaming-partial output_tokens, redaction.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: I am not aware of published work using provider prompt-token deltas as a content-length witness for agent tool logs. Not checked.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Gemini IMAGE-token screenshot ledger
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: dIMAGE / per-model unit must equal the number of screenshot-returning actions in the window (5059 / 5092 gui windows positive, 0 in all non-gui windows; values are always 0 or one unit).
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: The 33 gui windows (5092 - 5059) with no image increment are unexplained. Needs promptTokensDetails, which only Gemini returns here.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: likely novel as a fabrication check. Not checked.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Unlogged-injection detector (positive-residual tail)
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Flag windows where the model received many more tokens than the log shows (e.g. ToolSearch median +890 tokens with 0 logged chars; aiv_cu pause dC p99 28144 with 23 logged chars).
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Known harness expansions (tool schemas, skill bodies), images, persisted-output previews (+104 median).
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: auditing for hidden context injections by token accounting may be new. Not checked.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Codex truncation-cap consistency
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: For Codex results above about 60k chars, dC - out_k must sit at the cap (median 11611, p5-p75 11602-11628). Smaller results must scale at about 3.6-3.8 chars/token.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Few large-result pairs (14 in [100k,300k)); the cap may change with Codex version or config.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: a scaffold-specific plausibility check, probably not described before. Not checked.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Server-id skew bracket (third clock)
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Decode the server-minted ids: Anthropic req/msg (UUIDv7 in base58), OpenAI item hex time, Gemini responseId LE seconds. Per stream (session x agent), compute L = max(last input ts - id time) and U = min(first block ts - id time). Flag the stream if L - U > 2 s (3 s for second-resolution ids). Honest baseline: 10/3,676 swechat streams, 1/847 cc_local, 0 in aiv_cu Anthropic/Gemini, 3/463 aiv_cu OpenAI.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Re-stamped resume or fork copies explain 2 of the 10 swechat inconsistent sessions; the other 8 are unexplained. Further sources: client clock steps within a stream, layout misdetection (chance-decoded random ids; mitigated by the 1-day rule and the v7/variant check), and corpora without server ids (aiv_cc, pre-switch msg-only logs). Not cryptographic: anyone who knows the layout can mint consistent ids.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Time-in-identifier forensics (UUIDv1, ULID, Snowflake) is a known general technique. Using LLM vendor request and response ids as an independent server clock to bracket agent tool-log timestamps may not be described; I did not check the literature.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Copy arbitration by embedded server time
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: For an id that appears in more than one log (resume, fork, mirror), compute each copy's event-ts minus id-time offset. The copy inside [-2 s, 10 min] is the original. In honest data, 178/178 split cases point to the earlier copy, with offsets of at least 619,473 ms against 2,347-21,734 ms.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Tiny n (2 re-stamped session pairs, split B only). A re-stamp smaller than 10 min would leave both copies plausible. Only works where request ids exist.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED; I am not aware of prior use for agent transcripts.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Id-format epoch (anachronism) check
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Classify each id's structure (random 128-bit, UUIDv4 shape, UUIDv7; OpenAI hex48 or hex50) and compare it with the claimed event date. Flag a post-switch format before the switch date, or a pre-switch format well after it. Switch points in this data: Anthropic msg 2026-07-06 20:23:44-20:37:04 UTC; OpenAI items 2025-09; toolu UUIDv4 shape by 2026-09.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: The rollout overlap window (81 old-format ids after the first new one). Bedrock and Vertex variants with unmeasured rollout dates. Switch dates are estimated from these corpora only. A chance UUIDv4 shape occurs at 1/64 for random ids.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Dating artifacts by format version is common in forensics. I have not seen it applied to LLM API ids.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Ordinal counters in tool-call ids
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: For id styles 'tool:N' and 'call-<uuid>-N', check N == the call's 1-based ordinal in the session, with every step +1 (1,511/1,511 and 578/578 in honest data). Any deleted, inserted or reordered call breaks it.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: None observed. Coverage is narrow: compat-chat models only, 58 sessions. Behaviour across context truncation or a resume is unmeasured.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Cross-reference closure of text-borne ids
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: Every id quoted in model-visible text must resolve to an earlier issuance of the same object in the session: agentId to the nested agent, notification tool-use-id to the issuing call, output-file name to the task id, spill-path id to its own call, Codex write_stdin session id to a live process, and commit sha to the same subject in git log. Honest mismatch counts are 0 for the first four; commit subjects disagree 6+4 of 3,056.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: References issued in a parent or earlier session (notifications 93 swechat and 637 cc_local; Codex 88 never issued; TaskOutput 16). Release redaction. Issuance text the regexes miss in newer harness versions. amend/rebase for commits. This needs session lineage before it can serve as an alarm.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Referential-integrity checking is standard in general; its application to agent transcripts is likely not new.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Session-scoped id segment as splice detector
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: All OpenAI hex50 item ids in a session share the first 16 hex digits (472/472 sessions, 0 shared across sessions). An item spliced in from another session would carry a different segment.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: None observed. The segment's semantics are unknown, so a provider-side change could alter it. aiv_cu OpenAI only.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED.

candidate_mechanisms.name: Server-internal request/message ordering
candidate_mechanisms.measurement: For responses whose request id and message id are both UUIDv7: msg_time - req_time must be >= 0 (observed min 44 ms, 0 negative of 30,680), and the mapping must be 1:1.
candidate_mechanisms.false_positive_source: Only post-switch message ids. In swechat, 14 requests carry more than 1 message id (retries or streaming restarts), so 1:1 is not universal.
candidate_mechanisms.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED.

skeptic_overclaims.text: O3: 'far more common than at nearby shifted times' is not supported. The lens's own per-shift rates are 0.536 at -2h, 0.473 at +2h and 0.510 at -4h, against 0.566 observed. The 0.259 local-null excess comes mostly from the +-1d shifts, which are ~0 because SEC county reports sit on a single UTC day. With a +-2h/4h-only null the excess is ~0.10 (my 0.102 [0.042, 0.181] with source-day clusters), and against the immediately preceding hours it is ~0.03.

O3: the per-source figures (SEC 0.423, USAspending 0.369, MAX 0.393, Clark 0.675, IHME 0.595) are excess over the local null, not before-window rates. The actual before rates are 0.994, 0.764, 0.833, 0.800 and 0.909, and after rates are similar or higher for MAX, Clark and IHME.

O3: the page-clustered CI [0.481, 0.655] treats pages as independent even though events share campaign bursts. With source-day clusters (36), before-obs is 0.555 [0.094, 0.894]. SEC county alone accounts for 80% of before-window hits.

O3/O4: these show source-specific co-activity at the campaign/day scale (permutation excess ~0.33). They do not show the hour-scale precedence that the 'which source was being worked when' framing suggests.

O7: 'almost all same-second groups contain a single data source' is mostly compositional. A within-minute source shuffle already gives 3899/4130 single-source groups against 3998 observed. The same-second clustering itself is a real excess.
O8: the median of about -80 s mixes clock offset and compose latency, so it does not independently show the save clock is UTC 'to within about a minute'. O10 (-1 s) is the real cross-check.

O11: the 'guessed now without reading a clock' reading is weak. 13/26 round after-save stamps are more than 1h ahead and 6/26 more than 1 day ahead, which fits hand-picked round IDs. The 26 come from 9 labels, 18 from one anonymous label.
O2: 'all on 4 heavily edited shared pages' is really 68/72 on one page (dse/WillkommenImWiki).

A6-O7: the claim that 'the total jumps down' is false. total_token_usage is unchanged in 57/57 sample breaks and 615/615 full breaks. 45/57 breaks are duplicate token_count emissions; the other 12 follow a compaction or rollback. Only those 12 match the I1a magnitudes. This is an artifact, not a surprise.

A6-O3: 'the IR drops' is false for OpenCode state.time.end (the loader uses it as the result ts), Codex exec/MCP duration (loader extra.duration_s) and AI Village updated_at (load_aiv_cu extra). The lens's own flagged[] marked these loader_pair or loader_leaf. AI Village updated_at is also within 1 ms of created_at in 19992/20000 rows, so it is not an independent clock.

A6-O1: the rate comes from the sample. The full-population rate 0.9954 [0.9947, 0.9960] falls outside the sample's cluster CI [0.997, 1.0]. All 402 full-population mismatches are harness display formats (persisted-output previews, offset warnings, dedup references) or dataset redaction. The cc_local result covers main sessions only.

A6-O2 JSON: the uncheckable Agent results (no nested traffic) are stored as match 94/94, rate 1.0, with a Wilson CI. This encodes a non-check as a pass. In the full population 24.5% of Agent results cannot be checked.

A6-O17: events data.cost is a 0/1 flag (18989 ones, 302 zeros), not a cost. inputTokens and outputTokens copy the provider usage block in the same row (5515/5515), so they are not an independent record.
A6-O8: the null is correct as stated. A post-hoc fit leaving out reasoning holds 618/633, so this is formula misspecification, not proof that no token identity exists.
A6-O12: 'always exactly -1' holds only in the sample. Full-population diffs range from -27 to 70.
A6-O9: the tool field is 0 in every row, so the identity reduces to total = input + output + thoughts.
A6-O15: the head is a uniform sample of rows, not time-uniform. The ordering and month checks support that it is row-uniform.

Notes Part 2: the harness token tally is called an 'exact, independent second bookkeeping'. It is a deterministic recount of the transcript's own usage fields. It adds only commit-time tamper-evidence for usage records and message deletion, not independent evidence about tool results.

T3: 'Most unmatched tallies are a dataset join artifact'. Across the 4 scaffolds the substitution resolves 31 of 64 (48%); only for Claude format alone is it most (28 of 42). The stated mechanism also fails for 8 of the 39 substituted sessions, which the table tally already matched (7 full, 1 prefix).

T4: residuals 'concentrated in ... dev/old CLI builds' is not supported. The residual rate is highest in 0.5.x, 15/1048 = 0.0143 [0.0087, 0.0235]. It is 0.0030 [0.0017, 0.0053] for 0.4.x and 0.0055 [0.0021, 0.0141] for dev.

T2: 'window class fully accounted for by the declared offset' holds only from window to offset. 158 full-class sessions also declare checkpoint_transcript_start, yet their tally covers the whole transcript.
T8: most of the 2504/2510 equality comes from single-session checkpoints, where it is close to a tautology. Only the 390/394 multi-session sums test aggregation.

T10: the out-of-cwd edit share 0.049 is conditional on sessions with at least one in-cwd edit and non-empty files_touched. Over all sessions with edits it is 0.084 [0.073, 0.095], with 995 of the 2412 out-of-cwd paths under /.claude/. Also, 'files_touched = committed files' fails in 13% of sessions (files_touched ⊄ commit files), so 'git-side bookkeeping' is approximate.
T12: 'no spikes' depends on the lens's spike definition. A rule fixed in advance (a value at or above 100 repeated at least 5 times) finds 2 mechanical cache_read repeats in Claude Code.

O1: 'Coverage differs by scaffold' does not survive repo clustering. opencode (one repo holds 489 of 624 sessions) and codex (8 repos) have repo-clustered CIs [0.438,0.882] and [0.111,0.872], which overlap claude_code [0.590,0.792].

O4: 'formatter-heavy languages' as a cause is unsupported. The Go excess is one repo, entireio/cli (0.228); in the other 14 Go repos the rate is 0.066 [0.032,0.105], below average. Whitespace normalization neutralizes gofmt alignment. Languages formatted by prettier or black are below average. Half of the worktree calls are the same repo. 'Most contradicted-looking Edits have mechanical causes' rests on one demonstrated mechanism, the partial-line edge rule (35% rescued); the rest are correlates.
O4: css 0.397 and kt 0/397 are sample noise. In the population, css is 0.194 [0.043,0.397] and kt is 29/768.

O4: the POST-HOC edge-substring rule was reported without a decoy. With the 8-character minimum, decoy inflation is small: cross-repo 125 -> 183 of 7714, same repo 261 -> 365 of 7782. Without the minimum the decoy jumps to 1700/7714, so the 8-character guard must be stated as part of the rule.

O5: the residual is small (148 calls in the population, 53 in the lens) mainly because the Bash flag counts any later command mentioning the file basename, which includes git add <file>, as an explanation. Without that flag the residual is 1024 calls in 276 sessions.

O3: 'the decoy fixes the chance-match level' holds only for cross-repo chance. Same-repo other-file (0.007) and prior-commit same-path (0.019) nulls are higher, though still far below the 0.83 real rate.
O10: 'mostly for honest reasons' treats co-occurring flags (any later rebase or reset in the session, any commit_not_found checkpoint) as causes; 33 to 39% of unmatched claims carry no flag.

O11: 'None found' for the mechanism is wrong. 15 of 19 population cases, and 6 of the lens's own 9, are re-reads (cat/tail) of earlier background-task output files, and 1 is an explicit GIT_COMMITTER_DATE amend. The 'replayed output' shape is mostly honest re-reading, and a call-window detector would false-alarm on it.
O12: the denominator of 6998/13424 includes 1134 pairs with null duration (no_span); among pairs with a span it is 6998/12290.

O8: 'These hidden calls are why duration_api_ms > duration_ms is common' is not supported. Main-only runs are all v2.1.38 and long (median 103 responses); non-main runs are mostly v2.0.77 and short (median 2). Within non-main runs api<=dur goes from 0/95 (short) to 43/56 (long). api-dur does not track non-main output tokens (Spearman -0.07, CI -0.26 to 0.13) or cost (-0.16, CI -0.33 to 0.04).

Denominator inflation (O1, O4, O5, O8): the '211 runs with >=1 API response' include 18 synthetic-only runs with zero usage and zero API time. O8's 39/39 is really 21/21 non-synthetic. O5's 265/265 includes 72 rows that are trivially 0==0 (non-trivial 193/193). O4 has 57 runs with zero user rows (non-trivial 153/154). O8's 172/211 is 172/193 over runs with real API calls.

O10: 'village MCP tools range from -40.3 to +35.7' leaves out mcp__village__search_history at -222.7 (n=146) in the lens's own JSON (-246.6 under the pre-registered fit). The per-tool means and |residual|/delta quantiles come from the post-hoc 5-term fit but are not labelled as such.

O11: the 898.8 tokens/image level comes from the post-hoc extended fit, which is not flagged in O11. Under the pre-registered fit it is 890.1, under a no-intercept model about 1112. The narrow CI covers resampling only, not model choice.

O6: Spearman 0.9975 between hidden output and summary chars mostly reflects how many compactions each run had (n_compactions alone gives 0.989-0.990). The per-compaction figure is 0.923 (0.854-0.953).
O2: Pearson 0.930 is tail-driven (0.727 with the top 1% of gaps removed). The 162.1 chars/s level depends on counting tool names as chars (132.8 without them; text blocks only 159.4).

O7 understates rather than overclaims: all 15 discrepant runs are explained exactly by non-null-stop responses missing from result.usage (12/12 by subset-sum, plus the 3 all-zero runs). Whether they are dropped depends on SDK version and date (v2.1.38 6/6 runs; v2.0.77 only on 2026-02-03), so it is not an 'association only, incomplete rule'.

Notes interpretation: 'cost and tokens cannot be edited independently' overstates a client-side arithmetic identity, since both can be rewritten together. The O3 durations and created_at are both client-written, so their agreement is internal consistency, not an independent witness.
D12: 'identical outputs thousands of times' — the payloads share a length and template, but the 1568 x 3764-char payloads hold 446 distinct texts, and no exact text repeats more than 59 times.
D3: 'two sizes on pro' — the lattice constant is set by model generation (2.5-pro → 258, 3.x-pro → 1064), and a third constant, 2160 (3 sessions), explains the whole 0.7% residual.

D7: 'one or two constants per harness, set by harness version' — inside the single swechat CC harness the constant changes with the model (4.6/4.7 → 1, 4.5 → 8/10, haiku-4-5 none), and aiv_cc's Opus 4.5 matches swechat's opus-4-5.

D2: '40 model turns + 1 synthetic' and 'cap' — 12% of 41-turn sessions have no synthetic turn, 9% of all sessions exceed 41 turns (max 326), and the spike's share changes by month; 'censored, not completions' is unmeasured.
D9: '0-4 ms jitter' — only 79% of gaps fall in [1000, 1004]; the claimed 0.877 is the [1000, 1010] window, and 7.6% of gaps are under 1000 ms.

D4: the PreToolUse contrast (4/644 vs 5588/26323) is a between-session confound: fast Edits inside plateau sessions also lack PreToolUse (5/430). One session holds 27% of plateau calls, and the post-hook timing rests on 376/644 calls.

D5: the cause is understated — the failure-cap truncation is measured (marker '[N characters truncated]', 5k head plus 5k tail, keyed to the error flag). The 30,000 success cap is overstated: it is unseen in swechat and rests on 3 cc_local values.
D19: 'always precedes' ignores the 1 s resolution of the HTTP Date header (415 flash and 1714 pro rows are ambiguous), and the direction is expected by construction.
D11: the 8192 spike is in aiv_cu anthropic-opus (12 values, 2 sessions), not in swechat CC, where it is listed.
D15: 'sleep 709/709 whole seconds' covers only sleeps ≥ 10 s; 71/1635 sleeps are fractional.
D1: 'almost all lattice hits from gpt-5.4' is mostly base rate; gpt-5.4-mini's per-row rate (0.030) is as high as gpt-5.4's, and the real contrast is gpt-5.3-codex (0.001).
D10: the Hill CI omits sensitivity to k (α 0.58-1.36 across reasonable k). New finding: 435/611 top-1% shell latencies run past their own timeout, so this tail is not execution time.

O9: 'Not mechanical.' Most of the CC-family error clustering is harness cascades within one response: sibling cancellation, interrupts and permission denials. swechat CC drops from 0.197 to 0.041 [0.031, 0.051], cc_local from 0.129 to 0.057 [-0.018, 0.093] and aiv_cc from 0.052 to 0.010 once those are removed and only cross-response pairs are kept. So candidate witness #3 (error-burst statistic) mostly measures harness structure.

O11: 'The shorter turnaround is unexplained.' At call level it is a gap_input artifact: 52% of calls in swechat CC multi-call responses take their 'latest input' from a sibling's own result. Per response, turnaround vs ncalls is only -0.132 (swechat CC) and -0.089 (cc_local), and input-to-last-block time is flat (-0.010).

O15 / notes A2 and A3: aiv_cc lat_ms vs stderr_len (-0.504) is coded U. stderr there is one constant 93-character harness notice ('Shell cwd was reset...') whose frequency rises over time (0% to 23.5% to 78.5% by month). It should be coded H.
O7: the swechat figures (within-tool 0.356, resp_ctx 0.426) use the running-max gap_input that O3 calls contaminated. Stream-aware values are 0.243 and 0.390.

O6: 'stable, harness-specific rate' is overstated. The rate depends on the model (Haiku 397, Opus 168, Sonnet 182 chars/s; CC subagent copies 336). It also depends on the predecessor: after another call in the same response, cc_local runs at about 1,270 chars/s with within-tool rho 0.32. The clock holds mainly for text/thinking-to-tool_use transitions.

O3: 'subagent turns are still faster' leaves out model mix. 41% of swechat CC subagent calls are Haiku, against 0.5% of main calls. Without Haiku the stream-aware rho is -0.217 [-0.246, -0.193], not -0.385. O3 also gives the pooled-swechat -0.539 as the CC value; CC alone is -0.550.

O10: 'no mechanism' and 'replicates across independent corpora'. All three replicating corpora are the Claude Code harness family. In cc_local most of the coupling runs through arg_len (partial 0.083). The residual is about 0.15 to 0.16 in single-call responses. It is absent where lat is execution start to end (OpenCode).
O13: 'context does not grow with position in cc_local' is wrong for the main thread (0.706). The null comes from one position index over merged fresh-context subagent streams.

O1 / notes B2.1: 'This alone produces nerr_rate-shell_share -0.897.' With null counted as no error the correlation is still -0.659, so the coverage artifact inflates it and does not create it. The mechanism is also specific to the built-in Bash tool: mcp__village__bash has non-null native_error on only 66 of 2,753 results.

O8: the Codex weakness is put down to unified-exec deferral. exec_command alone agrees at 0.913. The pooled 0.444 (19 sessions) is driven by MCP tools (about 0) and by composition across tool_raws, with write_stdin deferral (0.535) as only one part. The CC clock comparison covers only 2.8% of CC calls (subagent, glob, webfetch and websearch).

O16: 'synthetic turns go with GUI-heavy sessions' is mostly between-model composition (-0.442 raw, -0.109 within model_string; n_synthetic is set by API shape). n_calls vs talk_share is compositional. 'Capped near 41-42' is a mode, not a cap: 43% of sessions have fewer than 40 turns.

O2: the cc_local subagent placeholder share (0.242) is essentially one session, which holds 6,615 of the 7,027 placeholder calls. O5 understates concentration: one session holds 45.9% of all cc_local/B calls and the top three hold 84.9%.

O7 and the 'Context-drop accounting' mechanism: '0 sharp unexplained drops' / '0/350 residue' only looked at CPs with no primary harness event.
